identity.title: Older Ages for 23 Pre-main Sequence Stars in Upper Scorpius Using Dynamical-mass-constrained Stellar Evolutionary Models

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present revised stellar ages for 23 pre-main sequence K- and M-type stars in the Upper Scorpius star-forming region, derived by using stellar dynamical masses to constrain isochronal ages from five pre-main sequence stellar evolutionary models.

We conducted high-sensitivity follow-up observations of these targets in ALMA Cycle 7, in which we targeted CO J $=$ 3 $-$2 line emission and 345 GHz continuum (Project 2019.1.00493.S, PI: P. Sheehan).

question.value: Derive revised stellar ages for 23 pre-main sequence K- and M-type stars in Upper Scorpius by using CO-derived stellar dynamical masses to constrain isochronal ages from five pre-main sequence stellar evolutionary models.

evidence.quote: We present revised stellar ages for 23 pre-main sequence K- and M-type stars in the Upper Scorpius star-forming region, derived by using stellar dynamical masses to constrain isochronal ages from five pre-main sequence stellar evolutionary models.
In this work, we use these dynamical masses to constrain the stellar age predictions of five PMS model sets, and thus derive mass-constrained isochronal ages for each target.

We conducted high-sensitivity follow-up observations of these targets in ALMA Cycle 7, in which we targeted CO J $=$ 3 $-$2 line emission and 345 GHz continuum (Project 2019.1.00493.S, PI: P. Sheehan).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00493.S.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive unconstrained isochronal masses and ages

method.value: Generate 10,000-point Gaussian distributions in T_eff and L_bol for each source, linearly interpolate onto five PMS evolutionary track grids (BHAC15, PARSEC v1.1, PARSEC v1.2S, Feiden 2016 non-magnetic and magnetic), and compute median and 1.4826*MAD of the resulting mass and age distributions.

evidence.quote: for each source, we generate Gaussian distributions in stellar temperature and luminosity using the Python package `numpy.random.normal`.

We feed these $T_{\rm eff}$ and $L_{\rm bol}$ into each set of evolutionary tracks using linear interpolation between the grid points, and obtain corresponding distributions of isochronal $M_{\star}$ and $\tau$.

We take the median of the $M_{\star}$ and $\tau$ distributions as the isochronal masses and ages, respectively. We take as our uncertainties the scaled median absolute deviation (1.4826$\times$MAD)[^1] of the $M_{\star}$ and $\tau$ distributions.

evidence.quote: The median age of Luhman-selected sample of K- and M-stars is 8$\pm$4 Myr both with and without the “pile-up” sources.

findings_qualitative.value: Applying a dynamical-mass constraint to isochronal ages increases stellar ages for standard non-magnetic models (from 3-5 Myr to 6-9 Myr), bringing low-mass K- and M-type star ages into agreement with the 8-11 Myr age of Upper Sco derived from early-type stars.

evidence.quote: We find that mass-constrained stellar ages for all model sets are more consistent with the older, $\sim$8-11 Myr age for Upper Sco derived using earlier-type stars.
Most standard (nonmagnetic) models produce younger ages (3-5 Myr) when unconstrained, but older ages (6-9 Myr) when constrained by dynamical mass.

findings_qualitative.value: Applying a dynamical-mass constraint reduces the scatter in derived age between different PMS evolutionary model sets at both the population level and the individual source level (for 14 of 17 sources).

evidence.quote: In contrast, the median mass-constrained ages span a narrower range (6 to 12 Myr), agree within uncertainties in all cases, and in fact are identical for three of the five model sets (9 Myr).
At the individual source level, we find a decrease in $\sigma_\tau$ for 14 out of the 17 sources that have at least two mass-constrained ages.

findings_qualitative.value: The Feiden (2016) magnetic models are the most reliable of the five tested PMS model sets, yielding 9-10 Myr median ages regardless of whether the dynamical mass constraint is applied.

evidence.quote: Models that account for global magnetic fields consistently produce the best match to our observations: they change comparatively little when the mass constraint is applied, and produce 9-10 Myr ages under both unconstrained and mass-constrained conditions.

evidence.loc: Overall Evaluation of the PMS Model Sets
evidence.quote: we conclude that the magnetic models of (cite: Feiden2016) are the most reliable isochronal method (of the five examined in this work) for determining stellar mass and age in the absence of independent mass constraints.

findings_qualitative.value: Four of the five PMS model sets (all except PARSEC v1.2S) exhibit consistent non-linear mass-dependent inaccuracies: tending to overestimate mass and age at M_* <= 0.25 M_sun, most severely underestimating mass and age around 0.25-0.6 M_sun, and improving toward >= 0.75 M_sun.

evidence.quote: Four of the five models (excepting PARSEC v1.2S) show the same mass-dependent behavior: the models are most likely to overestimate mass and age for $M_{\star}$ $\lesssim$ 0.25 M$_{\odot}$, they are most likely underestimate mass and age for $M_{\star}$ $\sim$0.5 M$_{\odot}$, and they show improved agreement with dynamical results as $M_{\star}$ rises to $\gtrsim$ 0.75 M$_{\odot}$.

findings_qualitative.value: The 23-star dynamical-mass sample shows no statistically significant age bias relative to the broader Upper Sco K- and M-type population (~2000-2500 stars).

evidence.loc: Testing for Age Bias in Our Sample
evidence.quote: Regardless of which Upper Sco selection criteria are used, and regardless of the inclusion/exclusion of the grid-edge sources, we find no statistically-significant difference between our dynamical-mass sample and the broader Upper Sco population.

findings_qualitative.value: The ~2x increase in low-mass stellar ages when constrained by dynamical masses supports literature findings that median protoplanetary disk lifetimes are ~2x longer than previously thought, providing >= 4 Myr of additional time for planet formation.

evidence.quote: We find that the typical increase in median stellar age from standard models ($\sim$2$\times$ when the mass constraint is applied) is consistent with literature findings that suggest a median disk lifetime of $\sim$2$\times$ previous estimates (cite: Fang2025). Our results suggest that planet-formation timescales may thus be $\gtrsim$4 Myr longer than previously thought.

claims.hypothesis: Purely isochronal methods systematically underestimate ages for low-mass (K- and M-type) pre-main sequence stars in Upper Sco, causing the apparent age discrepancy with earlier-type stars (~5 Myr vs ~8-11 Myr).
claims.experiment: Derive unconstrained and CO-dynamical-mass-constrained isochronal ages for 23 K- and M-type stars in Upper Sco across five PMS evolutionary model sets (BHAC15, PARSEC v1.1, PARSEC v1.2S, Feiden 2016 non-magnetic and magnetic).
claims.result: Unconstrained median ages for standard models (BHAC15, PARSEC v1.1, Feiden 2016 non-magnetic) are 3-5 Myr, whereas dynamical-mass-constrained median ages increase to 6-9 Myr (and 6-12 Myr across all five models), with median age ratios tau_all/tau_dyn of 0.6-0.7 for standard models.
claims.finding: Applying a dynamical-mass constraint increases derived ages for standard PMS models by ~1.4-1.67x, bringing low-mass star ages into alignment with the 8-11 Myr Upper Sco age from early-type stars.

evidence.quote: The median unconstrained ages for the BHAC15, PARSEC v1.1, and non-magnetic (cite: Feiden2016) models are 5$\pm$1, 3$\pm$1, and 5$\pm$1 Myr, respectively.
When the mass constraint is applied, stellar age shows a strong tendency to increase. The median mass-constrained ages rise to 6$-$12 Myr, depending on the model set.

Moreover, this constraint brings most model sets into closer alignment with the older, 8-11 Myr age long derived for Upper Sco using early-type sources, and appears to ease, if not resolve, the longstanding age discrepancy for this region.

claims.hypothesis: Applying an independent dynamical-mass constraint reduces the discordance between different PMS evolutionary model sets.
claims.experiment: Compare the population median age range and individual intra-source age spread (sigma_tau = tau_max - tau_min) across the five PMS model sets before and after applying the dynamical mass constraint.
claims.result: The range of population median ages narrows from 3-14 Myr (unconstrained) to 6-12 Myr (mass-constrained, with three models at 9 Myr), and median intra-source age spread drops from 11+/-6 Myr to 8+/-7 Myr, decreasing for 14 of 17 individual sources.
claims.finding: Dynamical mass constraints significantly increase agreement among PMS evolutionary models at both the population and individual source levels.

evidence.quote: In contrast, the median mass-constrained ages span a narrower range (6 to 12 Myr), agree within uncertainties in all cases, and in fact are identical for three of the five model sets (9 Myr).
The median age spread decreases from 11$\pm$6 Myr to 8$\pm$7 Myr.
At the individual source level, we find a decrease in $\sigma_\tau$ for 14 out of the 17 sources that have at least two mass-constrained ages.

claims.hypothesis: PMS evolutionary models that include global magnetic fields provide more accurate unconstrained mass and age predictions than standard non-magnetic models.
claims.experiment: Evaluate the change in median age, age ratio (tau_all/tau_dyn), mass accuracy, and population scatter across all five PMS model sets when the dynamical mass constraint is applied.
claims.result: The Feiden (2016) magnetic models yield median ages of 10+/-5 Myr (unconstrained) and 9+/-5 Myr (mass-constrained), with a median age ratio tau_all/tau_dyn of 1.0+/-0.3 and median Delta tau of 0+/-3 Myr, and only 5/23 sources lacking mass overlap.
claims.finding: The Feiden (2016) magnetic models are the most reliable of the five model sets for determining PMS mass and age without independent mass constraints, though they still exhibit non-linear mass-dependent trends at low masses.

evidence.quote: Models that account for global magnetic fields consistently produce the best match to our observations: they change comparatively little when the mass constraint is applied, and produce 9-10 Myr ages under both unconstrained and mass-constrained conditions.

evidence.loc: Overall Evaluation of the PMS Model Sets
evidence.quote: Based on our findings in the previous sections, and our results in (cite: Towner2025), we conclude that the magnetic models of (cite: Feiden2016) are the most reliable isochronal method (of the five examined in this work) for determining stellar mass and age in the absence of independent mass constraints.

claims.hypothesis: The 23 disk-bearing K- and M-type stars with CO dynamical masses are representative in age of the broader Upper Sco low-mass stellar population.
claims.experiment: Compare the Feiden (2016) magnetic age distribution of the 23-star sample against 2059 (Luhman 2022 criteria) and 2469 (Ratzenböck et al. 2023a criteria) K- and M-type Upper Sco stars from Fang & Herczeg (2025) using 2-sample KS and Anderson-Darling tests.
claims.result: The broader K- and M-type population has a median age of 7-8+/-4 Myr (consistent with 10+/-5 Myr unconstrained and 9+/-5 Myr constrained for the 23-star sample), with KS test p-values of 0.006 to 0.09 and Anderson-Darling p-values of 0.002 to 0.05.
claims.finding: The 23-star dynamical-mass sample is not significantly age-biased relative to the overall Upper Sco K- and M-type population.

evidence.loc: Testing for Age Bias in Our Sample

evidence.loc: Testing for Age Bias in Our Sample
evidence.quote: We thus conclude that our derived $\sim$9 Myr age for Upper Sco using our dynamical-mass constrained, K- and M-type PMS stars is robust against sample age bias.

why_this_data.value: Upper Sco is the nearest massive star-forming region, exhibits a well-known age discrepancy between early- and late-type stars, and hosts tens of CO-detectable gas disks around K- and M-type stars suitable for Keplerian dynamical mass measurements.

evidence.quote: Its overall well-studied nature, seemingly mass-dependent inferred ages, and large population of CO-detectable disks make Upper Sco an excellent candidate for a systematic calibration of isochronal ages by dynamical methods.

why_this_method.value: Keplerian disk fitting yields dynamical masses but not ages directly; combining dynamical masses with HRD positions (T_eff, L_bol) across multiple PMS evolutionary tracks enables a direct comparison between unconstrained and mass-constrained isochronal ages.

evidence.quote: A more direct comparison, however, would be between a purely isochronal age and a mass-constrained age for all PMS models.

Keplerian fitting of the protostellar disk does not directly yield a stellar age. Therefore, following methods established in the literature (cite: Soderblom2014; Rizzuto2016; David2019), we use five pre-main sequence evolutionary tracks to derive two stellar ages for each source:

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Lithium depletion boundary (LDB) and other age methods omitted from literature comparison because they are less accurate for the young (5-11 Myr) age range of Upper Sco.

evidence.loc: Comparison with Existing Literature for Upper Sco
evidence.quote: However, some methods are known to be less accurate for young and/or low-mass sources (cite: Soderblom2014). As Upper Sco is generally considered to be younger than this (5-11 Myr), we restrict our comparison to two alternate methods: eclipsing binaries and dynamical traceback modeling.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Starspot evolutionary models (e.g., SP15 / Somers et al.) were discussed as a plausible physical explanation for non-linear mass-dependent trends, but were not tested in this work.

evidence.loc: On the Consistency of Trends Across Model Sets
evidence.quote: A model that combines (global) magnetic fields with the observational color and temperature effects of (localized) starspots, then, could potentially be a fruitful avenue of future research. However, as we do not test any starspot models in this work, such a possibility is highly speculative at this time.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: PARSEC v1.2S models rejected as reliable for this mass and age range due to severe mass overestimation at low masses, large population age scatter, and non-systematic behavior.

evidence.loc: Overall Evaluation of the PMS Model Sets
evidence.quote: However, we do conclude that, for the mass and age range covered by our sample, the PARSEC v1.2S models are not as reliable as the other four model sets tested.

referee_caveats_inferred: All ALMA data reduction, imaging, and dynamical mass MCMC fitting were performed in the companion paper (Towner et al. 2025); any systematic bias in the CO dynamical masses (e.g., disk inclination degeneracies, surface density/temperature parameterization, or unresolved companions) directly propagates into the mass-constrained ages here.

Five out of 23 targets (22% of the sample, including all stars with M_dyn >= 1 M_sun) fail to produce a dynamical-mass-constrained age in any model set because the CO dynamical mass does not overlap the HRD-derived isochronal mass.

The sample consists exclusively of disk-bearing stars with surviving CO gas disks; although KS/AD tests against Fang & Herczeg (2025) HRD ages show no statistically significant difference, the p-values (0.002-0.09) are marginal and disk-bearing gas-rich stars could still represent a modestly younger or distinct subset.
